Its borrowing costs have reached their highest level in more than two decades.
Investors now demand higher yields on French government bonds than on Italian or Greek ones.

With parliament deeply divided and a presidential election approaching, agreeing on a solution is proving difficult.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Fears are growing that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spill over into neighbouring NATO members – and spread regionally.
Some countries would argue it already has – pointing to drone incursions, cyberattacks and sabotage.
European nations say Moscow is targeting Ukraine’s allies to intimidate them. The Kremlin denies the accusations.
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski warns Europe should be ready to respond robustly to Russia’s hybrid attacks.
Poland, which borders Ukraine, is home to a NATO logistics hub used for military and civilian support to its neighbour.
The International Centre for Counterterrorism says the country is the ‘primary focus’ of Russia’s sabotage campaign in Europe.
It’s also the country most targeted by cyberattacks, according to research from Harvard, with about four thousand politically motivated attacks per day.
And Poland is on heightened alert.
It’s reported several airspace violations -- and authorities say more drone and missile strikes are likely.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Thousands of students, professors and labour union members have taken to the streets of Buenos Aires to protest against Argentine President Javier Milei’s economic austerity plan, particularly cuts to public university funding.

The demonstrations near the Congress building escalated into clashes with police, who used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. Protesters say the cuts are undermining education quality, eroding salaries and threatening students’ ability to continue their studies.

Protester Agustin Romero criticised the impact of the cuts on education and pensions, while student Emiliano Gato described the difficulties students face as university funding comes under pressure.

Milei, speaking in New York, defended his economic programme, saying Argentina’s economy is growing rapidly and his reforms are helping to reduce inflation.
